findings.description: none: Live principal isolation test `test_exact_agent_and_service_policy_isolation` verifies least-privilege AppRole policies across agent and service principals against real OpenBao. Each agent reads only its own `agents/<name>` key and declared `vendors/<vendor>` key, `service-identity-reader` reads only agent keys, and `service-egress-gateway` reads only declared vendor keys. Cross-agent and cross-vendor access attempts raise `BaoCredentialError(ErrorCode.AUTHORIZATION_DENIED)`, and write or list attempts fail with `hvac.exceptions.Forbidden`.
findings.existing_code:
for client, path in ((alice, "agents/bob"), (alice, "vendors/openai"),
                         (bob, "agents/alice"), (bob, "vendors/anthropic"),
                         (identity, "vendors/anthropic"), (gateway, "agents/alice")):
        with pytest.raises(BaoCredentialError) as error:
            client.read_api_key(path)
        assert error.value.code == ErrorCode.AUTHORIZATION_DENIED
findings.resolution: No action needed; complies with D1, D3, D6, and Scenarios AI-06, AI-08, AI-11, AI-12, CFG-14.

findings.description: none: Periodic token renewal is demonstrated beyond the ordinary max lease TTL in `test_periodic_token_renews_past_auth_mount_max_ttl`. The auth mount max lease TTL is tuned to 5s while an AppRole is provisioned with `token_period="4s"` and `token_max_ttl="0s"`. The test performs periodic renewal over 6 seconds (3 intervals of 2s), confirming token identity retention (`client_token`), lease expiration extension, and successful key retrieval past the mount's 5s boundary. Mount tuning is safely restored in a finally block.
findings.existing_code:
for _ in range(3):
            time.sleep(2.0)
            renewed = _reader(live, role_name).ensure_session(principal_id, role_name)
            assert renewed.client_token == initial.client_token
            assert renewed.lease_expires_at > initial.lease_expires_at
        after_mount_max = _reader(live, role_name)
        after_mount_max.ensure_session(principal_id, role_name)
        assert after_mount_max.read_agent_key("alice") == "alice-secret"
findings.resolution: No action needed; complies with D3, D6, and OpenBao periodic token contract.

findings.description: none: Coordinator atomic identity snapshot rotation and degraded readiness are verified against real OpenBao in `test_coordinator_live_snapshot_rotation_and_readiness`. In-place key rotation in `agents/alice` takes effect on the next reload without process restart, and lookups for the rotated key resolve while the old key is immediately denied. Injected duplicate keys cause reload failure, entering degraded readiness while continuing to serve the previous valid snapshot during the grace period.
findings.existing_code:
assert runtime.reload()
        assert runtime.lookup("alice-secret") is None
        assert runtime.lookup("alice-rotated") is not None
        root.secrets.kv.v2.create_or_update_secret(path="agents/bob", secret={"api_key": "alice-rotated"}, mount_point="secret")
        assert not runtime.reload()
        assert runtime.readiness() == ("degraded", True)
        assert runtime.lookup("alice-rotated") is not None
findings.resolution: No action needed; complies with D4, D6, and Scenarios COORD-01, COORD-02, COORD-03, COORD-05, COORD-09.

findings.description: none: Langfuse internal credential helper migration (`langfuse_env.sh`) enforces strict credential boundaries. The helper uses `BAO_INTERNAL_ROLE_ID` and `BAO_INTERNAL_SECRET_ID` to log in and reads `secret/coordinator` under the isolated `coordinator-internal-read` policy. Legacy inputs `BAO_ROLE_ID` and `BAO_SECRET_ID` are completely ignored and cannot authenticate. Unit tests (`test_langfuse_env.py`) and live tests (`test_langfuse_internal_role_only_reads_coordinator`) verify that the internal AppRole cannot read agent paths (`agents/alice`) and legacy variables are not emitted.
findings.existing_code:
token="${BAO_TOKEN:-}"
        if [ -z "$token" ] && [ -n "${BAO_INTERNAL_ROLE_ID:-}" ] && [ -n "${BAO_INTERNAL_SECRET_ID:-}" ]; then
            token=$(curl -fsS \
                -X POST \
                -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
                --data "{\"role_id\":\"${BAO_INTERNAL_ROLE_ID}\",\"secret_id\":\"${BAO_INTERNAL_SECRET_ID}\"}" \
                "${bao_addr}/v1/auth/approle/login" \
                | sed -n 's/.*"client_token":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
        fi
findings.resolution: No action needed; complies with D5, tasks 5.6-5.7, and Scenario CFG-19.

findings.description: none: CI workflow wiring in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` introduces dedicated job `test-openbao-live` running on `ubuntu-latest`. It installs locked skill dependencies, runs isolated Langfuse helper tests, and executes `run_live_matrix.sh` using the container engine. The job runs independently of PostgREST integration fixtures with a 15-minute timeout.
findings.existing_code:
test-openbao-live:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7

      - name: Set up Python 3.12
        run: uv python install 3.12

      - name: Install locked skill dependencies
        run: uv sync --project skills --locked --all-extras

      - name: Test isolated Langfuse credentials helper
        run: skills/.venv/bin/python -m pytest skills/bao-vault/scripts/tests/test_langfuse_env.py -q

      - name: Run pinned live OpenBao conformance matrix
        run: bash skills/bao-vault/scripts/tests/integration/run_live_matrix.sh
findings.resolution: No action needed; complies with D6, task 5.8, and CI wiring requirements.

findings.description: none: Operator documentation in `docs/openbao-secret-management.md`, `agent-coordinator/.secrets.yaml.example`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `README.md` provides an exhaustive, safe staged cutover and rollback guide. It covers flat file staging for deployment vendor keys before preflight, 1:1 migration map specification, preflight dry-run execution, mode 0700/0600 file permission enforcement, internal role handoff with `BAO_INTERNAL_*` variables, `/ready` health gating, explicit cutover retirement via `--confirm-cutover` and `--internal-role-name`, release-level rollback via prior release and `secret/coordinator` backup, and troubleshooting for typed errors.
findings.existing_code: For final retirement, supply --confirm-cutover --internal-role-name <existing-internal-role> and matching BAO_INTERNAL_ROLE_ID and BAO_INTERNAL_SECRET_ID to the seeder. It verifies that this role reads secret/coordinator under the isolated policy and refuses unknown roles still using coordinator-read. Drain or restart processes holding old internal tokens before deleting the shared policy; a token issued before policy change can retain access until its lease ends.
findings.resolution: No action needed; complies with D3, D5, D6, and Scenarios CFG-07, CFG-08, CFG-09, CFG-12, CFG-13, CFG-17, CFG-18.

findings.description: nit: `run_live_matrix.sh` extracts the OpenBao image from `agent-coordinator/docker-compose.yml` via a multi-line `sed` regex pattern (`sed -n '/^  openbao:/,/^  [a-z]/s/^[[:space:]]*image: //p'`). This assumes standard two-space indentation and that the next top-level service block begins with a lowercase letter at column 2. While correct for the current Compose file, it is sensitive to formatting changes.
findings.resolution: Consider parsing the compose YAML file using Python `yaml` or `tomllib` if the file formatting changes in the future.

findings.description: optional: In `test_exact_agent_and_service_policy_isolation`, the negative authorization matrix checks cross-agent (`agents/bob`), cross-vendor (`vendors/openai`), and service-boundary denials (`identity` on `vendors/*`, `gateway` on `agents/*`), but does not include an explicit read attempt against `coordinator` for agent or service principals. While OpenBao's default deny model guarantees that paths outside the policy are inaccessible (and `coordinator-internal-read` is tested for agent denial in `test_langfuse_internal_role_only_reads_coordinator`), adding an explicit `client.read_api_key("coordinator")` assertion would directly verify AI-06 and AI-11's requirement that agents and service principals have no access to `secret/data/coordinator`.
